response.justification: Strong, broad engineer with 15+ years across web, backend, embedded and infrastructure, and directly relevant recent exposure to agentic development — currently building MCP code generators and AI-agent tooling at a Staff level. The Sociomantic/dunnhumby stint gives credible high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems experience (microservices handling millions of requests/second), and the GISCollective founder role demonstrates ownership, event-driven architecture and Kubernetes deployment. The main gap is the stated must-have: Python is absent from the skills list and every listed project, while the deep systems work was in D rather than the target stack. Evidence of technical strategy at scale, cross-functional stakeholder management, and formal on-call/incident ownership is also thin — the resume is craft- and delivery-oriented rather than strategy-oriented. Worth a screen to probe Python depth and scope of influence, but not an obvious yes on paper.
strengths: Hands-on agentic/AI tooling: MCP code generators and agent frameworks
Real high-throughput distributed systems experience (millions of req/sec)
Deep TypeScript/Node plus strong TDD, CI/CD and craftsmanship culture
concerns: No demonstrated Python — an explicit must-have for the role
Little evidence of technical strategy or cross-functional stakeholder leadership
Recent roles are product full-stack; scale/on-call ownership not evidenced
